function.mechanism: Displaces oxygen/air because of inert gas behavior, limiting oxidation and enabling propellant/aeration and cryogenic freezing applications.
common_food_categories: emulsified dressings packed in nitrogen/carbon dioxide atmospheres

adi.basis: No finalized EFSA ADI found; Open EFSA lists E941 re-evaluation as ongoing with no output adopted yet.

efsa.key_finding: Open EFSA question EFSA-Q-2011-00714 (updated 2026-01-19) states E941 is already authorized in the EU and scientific output preparation is ongoing after the 31/03/2024 data-call closure.

adi.basis: JECFA entry for Nitrogen (INS 941) states: NO ADI NECESSARY.

concerns.summary: Recent human literature includes acute gastric perforation case reports after ingestion of liquid-nitrogen beverages; this reflects misuse/handling hazard rather than a chronic toxicological signal for normal E941 additive exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA evaluated nitrogen (INS 941) with ADI outcome 'NO ADI NECESSARY' (1980).
No elemental nitrogen entry (name 'Nitrogen' or CAS 7727-37-9) was identified in the current IARC classifications dataset checked.
FDA affirms nitrogen as GRAS under 21 CFR 184.1540 with cGMP conditions.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI is set by JECFA (NO ADI NECESSARY), and no finalized EFSA ADI was found because EFSA re-evaluation remains ongoing.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence indicates low toxicological concern for normal food-additive use (JECFA: NO ADI NECESSARY; FDA GRAS). Main identified harms are acute misuse/handling events involving liquid nitrogen preparations, not chronic hazard from typical E941 exposure.
key_factors: JECFA ADI outcome: NO ADI NECESSARY
No elemental-nitrogen IARC carcinogenic classification identified
EFSA re-evaluation still ongoing without final scientific output
Recent PubMed evidence centers on acute misuse injuries
